name: Mechanical watch
title: Automatic mechanical dive watch
intro: This is a battery-free automatic mechanical watch. Explode it (🧩) to see the mainspring, gear train, escapement and balance wheel. Ask me "How does the mainspring move the hands?"
suggest: How does the mainspring move the hands?
Where does the tick-tock come from?
How does an automatic watch wind itself?
looksLike: watch, wristwatch, mechanical watch, dive watch, timepiece

case.name: Case
case.info: 42 mm stainless-steel housing that protects the movement and seals out water and dust.

crystal.name: Crystal
crystal.info: Clear sapphire crystal on top, extremely hard and scratch-resistant.

case_back.name: Case back
case_back.info: Screw-down back cover with a waterproof gasket; removing it reveals the movement.

bezel.name: Rotating bezel
bezel.info: Unidirectional anticlockwise bezel (120 clicks). Align 0 with the minute hand when diving; accidental knocks only shorten remaining dive time for safety.

crown.name: Crown
crown.info: Side knob connected via the winding stem: turn it to wind the mainspring by hand, or pull it out to set the hands.

dial.name: Dial
dial.info: The watch face with hour markers, sitting above the motion works and mainplate.

hour_hand.name: Hour hand
hour_hand.info: Shortest hand, geared down to turn once every 12 hours (1/12 the speed of the minute hand).

minute_hand.name: Minute hand
minute_hand.info: Mounted directly on the centre wheel arbor, turning once an hour.

seconds_hand.name: Seconds hand
seconds_hand.info: Mounted on the fourth wheel arbor, turning once a minute in 8 tiny steps per second.

mainplate.name: Main plate
mainplate.info: Base plate of the movement that holds the lower pivots of all the gears.

barrel.name: Mainspring barrel
barrel.info: Houses the coiled mainspring—the watch's sole power source—which slowly unwinds to turn the 84-tooth barrel gear once every 7 hours.

barrel_bridge.name: Barrel bridge
barrel_bridge.info: Bridge securing the top arbor of the mainspring barrel.

center_wheel.name: Centre wheel
center_wheel.info: Located at the centre of the movement and driven to turn once an hour, carrying the minute hand.

third_wheel.name: Third wheel
third_wheel.info: Intermediate gear that multiplies the centre wheel's speed by 7.5 to drive the fourth wheel.

fourth_wheel.name: Fourth wheel
fourth_wheel.info: Speeds up rotation further to turn once a minute, carrying the seconds hand on its arbor.

escape_wheel.name: Escape wheel
escape_wheel.info: Saw-toothed wheel that is locked and released one tooth at a time by the pallet fork to meter out the mainspring's power.

pallet_fork.name: Pallet fork
pallet_fork.info: Anchor-shaped lever that rocks left and right with the balance wheel, releasing the escape wheel one tooth at a time while giving the balance a tiny impulse push.

balance.name: Balance wheel
balance.info: Weighted wheel paired with a fine hairspring that oscillates at a steady 8 beats per second (4 Hz) to regulate timekeeping accuracy.

balance_cock.name: Balance cock
balance_cock.info: Cantilever bridge supporting the upper pivot of the balance wheel.

train_bridge.name: Train bridge
train_bridge.info: Bridge holding the upper pivots of the third, fourth and escape wheels.

minute_wheel.name: Minute wheel
minute_wheel.info: Reduction gear under the dial that slows the minute hand's rotation by 12 times to drive the hour hand.

rotor.name: Rotor
rotor.info: Half-disc weight on the back that swings with your wrist's motion, automatically winding the mainspring.

strap_top.name: Upper strap
strap_top.info: Upper watch strap at the 12 o'clock side.

strap_bottom.name: Lower strap
strap_bottom.info: Lower watch strap at the 6 o'clock side.

drives.tick: Balance wheel and pallet fork swinging (slowed down 8 times)

train.title: How the mainspring moves the hands

steps.say: The coiled steel mainspring slowly unwinds inside the barrel, turning the barrel gear about once every 7 hours.
The barrel gear drives the central pinion so the centre wheel—and the minute hand on it—turns once an hour.
Through the third wheel, rotation speeds up to spin the fourth wheel—and the seconds hand—once a minute.

quiz.q: Why does the seconds hand spin 60 times faster than the minute hand?
options: The gears multiply the speed stage by stage
From centre wheel to third wheel and third to fourth, each large gear driving a small pinion speeds rotation up, multiplying to 60.
The seconds hand has its own high-speed mainspring
The entire watch runs off a single mainspring barrel and one gear train.
Because the seconds hand is thinner and lighter
Gear ratios strictly lock the speed of each hand regardless of weight.

steps.say: Beneath the dial, the minute wheel steps the minute hand's speed down 12 times to turn the hour hand.

quiz.q: When the minute hand completes one full turn, how far does the hour hand move?
options: 1/12 of a turn (moving forward by one hour marker)
The minute hand must turn 12 times for the hour hand to turn once, moving one marker per hour.
One full turn as well
If both turned at the same speed, the hour and minute hands would always overlap.
Half a turn
Half a turn of the hour hand equals 6 hours; it only moves one marker per hour.

escapement.title: Tick-tock: the balance and the escapement

steps.say: Without a brake, the mainspring would unwind in seconds. The escape wheel and pallet fork lock and release the gear train step by step.
Driven by its hairspring, the balance wheel swings back and forth at a fixed 8 beats per second (shown here slowed down 8 times).
Each swing of the balance flicks the pallet fork, letting the escape wheel advance by a single tooth before locking it again—creating the tick-tock sound.

quiz.q: Which part determines how accurately a mechanical watch keeps time?
options: The balance wheel and hairspring
The balance-hairspring system oscillates at a constant natural frequency, and the escapement releases the gears strictly to that beat.
The mainspring barrel
The mainspring only supplies force; the balance wheel controls the rate at which that force is released.
The seconds hand
The seconds hand merely displays the rotation of the fourth wheel.

steps.say: As each escape tooth slips past, its angled tip gives the pallet fork and balance wheel a tiny push, replacing energy lost to friction.
Turning the side crown winds the mainspring inside the barrel via the stem—that's manual winding.
While worn, everyday wrist motion swings the weighted half-moon rotor on the back, winding the mainspring automatically.

quiz.q: What happens if you leave an automatic mechanical watch sitting still on a desk for three days?
options: The mainspring unwinds completely and the watch stops
Without wrist motion to spin the rotor, the stored spring energy runs out after about 40 hours.
It keeps running forever
Automatic winding harvests energy from your wrist movement; it isn't a perpetual motion machine.
It switches to backup battery power
A mechanical watch contains no battery or electronics.

steps.say: The outer dive bezel uses a one-way ratchet that turns anticlockwise only, preventing divers from accidentally underestimating their bottom time.

minute_wheel.title: Broken minute wheel
minute_wheel.short: The minute hand moves, the hour hand doesn't
minute_wheel.symptom: The watch is ticking and the seconds and minute hands turn normally, but the hour hand stays stuck in place. What's broken?
minute_wheel.hint: Which reduction gear under the dial slows the centre wheel's rotation by 12 times to drive the hour hand?
minute_wheel.observe: Since the seconds and minute hands move, the main gear train works. Look right under the dial at the gear connecting the minute hand to the hour hand.
whys: Watch the centre wheel, fourth wheel and seconds hand—they're all turning, proving the mainspring still has power.
Look at the balance wheel—it's still oscillating and the seconds hand is ticking. The break is right between the minute hand and hour hand.
minute_wheel.cause: The minute wheel under the dial is broken, so rotation from the centre wheel (minute hand) never reaches the hour hand.
minute_wheel.why: Why does the minute hand keep moving while the hour hand stays still when the minute wheel breaks?
minute_wheel.answer: The minute hand sits directly on the centre wheel, whereas the hour hand relies on the minute wheel to step that rotation down 12 times. When the minute wheel breaks, the hour hand receives no drive.
reasons: The minute wheel generates electricity for the hour hand.
The hour and minute hands are welded to the same solid shaft, so a broken minute wheel locks both hands.
